title: Why This Portfolio Has 7 Templates
excerpt: One JSON, many faces — and what that decision taught me about building systems.
content:
Most portfolios are a single design. Mine renders **7 templates** from one content source, and that was a deliberate decision.

## The Problem I Wanted to Solve

Every time I redesigned my site, I rewrote the content too. Copy got lost, sections drifted out of sync, and I lost motivation halfway through.

So I separated the two:

- Content lives in JSON
- Presentation lives in template components

## What That Unlocked

Adding a new look is now a folder of components — no content migration, no copy-paste. Switching between them is instant, and the choice is stored in the URL:

```
?template=glass&scheme=ocean&lang=en
```

## The Real Lesson

The templates are not the point. The point is that **structure beats effort**. Once content and presentation were separated, everything else — color schemes, three languages, a blog — became cheap to add.

> Build the system once, then the features are almost free.

## Trade-offs

Seven templates means seven places to fix a layout bug. I accept that cost because the alternative — one rigid design I get bored of — is worse.
